docs.title: Tusk Framework
docs.text:
Tusk is a PHP application framework for building HTTP APIs and services with an explicit application bootstrap and long-lived PHP workers.

The Tusk Engine is the Go control plane: it diagnoses project prerequisites, generates the RoadRunner runtime configuration at startup, and supervises the RoadRunner process. RoadRunner owns HTTP transport and the PHP worker pool. The Framework owns application bootstrap, routing, dependency injection, and request handling.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Requirements: PHP 8.2 or newer, Composer, the Tusk Engine, and a RoadRunner binary available to the Engine. See Installation for setup details.

composer create-project tusk-framework/app catalog
cd catalog
tusk doctor
tusk start

The sample app includes a small product API. Its data is in memory for demonstration; use a database-backed repository for persistent or shared state. See Your First App to try the endpoint.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Client → RoadRunner (HTTP + PHP workers) → Tusk Framework application
                    ↑
          supervised by Tusk Engine

The Engine manages runtime lifecycle; it is not a second HTTP server or worker pool. Read the architecture overview and Engine integration guide for the boundaries.

docs.title: Container API Reference
docs.text: The Container class is the heart of Tusk's dependency injection system.

docs.title: set(string $id, callable $factory): void
docs.text:
Register a service factory in the container.

Parameters: - $id (string) - Service identifier (typically the class name) - $factory (callable) - Factory function that returns the service instance

Example:

use Tusk\Core\Container\Container;

$container = new Container();

// Register a simple service
$container->set(LoggerInterface::class, function() {
    return new FileLogger('/var/log/app.log');
});

// Register with dependencies
$container->set(UserService::class, function(Container $c) {
    return new UserService(
        $c->get(UserRepository::class),
        $c->get(LoggerInterface::class)
    );
});

docs.title: get(string $id): mixed
docs.text:
Resolve and retrieve a service from the container.

Parameters: - $id (string) - Service identifier

Returns: The resolved service instance

Throws: ContainerException if service cannot be resolved

Example:

$logger = $container->get(LoggerInterface::class);
$logger->info('Application started');

docs.title: has(string $id): bool
docs.text:
Check if a service is registered in the container.

Parameters: - $id (string) - Service identifier

Returns: true if registered, false otherwise

Example:

if ($container->has(CacheInterface::class)) {
    $cache = $container->get(CacheInterface::class);
} else {
    // Use fallback
}

docs.title: Auto-Wiring
docs.text:
The container automatically resolves constructor dependencies using reflection.

Example:

class UserController
{
    public function __construct(
        private UserRepository $repo,
        private LoggerInterface $logger,
        private EventDispatcher $events
    ) {}
}

// No manual registration needed!
$controller = $container->get(UserController::class);
// Container automatically injects all dependencies

docs.title: Auto-Wiring Rules
docs.text:
1. Type-hinted parameters are resolved by their type
  2. Interfaces must be explicitly bound to implementations
  3. Scalar values cannot be auto-wired (use factory functions)
  4. Circular dependencies will throw an exception

docs.title: Singleton Pattern
docs.text:
Register services as singletons to reuse the same instance:

$container->set(DatabaseConnection::class, function() {
    static $instance = null;
    if ($instance === null) {
        $instance = new DatabaseConnection('mysql:host=localhost');
    }
    return $instance;
});

// Or use a helper method (if implemented)
$container->singleton(DatabaseConnection::class, function() {
    return new DatabaseConnection('mysql:host=localhost');
});

docs.title: Service Providers
docs.text:
Organize service registration using service providers:

use Tusk\Core\ServiceProviderInterface;

class DatabaseServiceProvider implements ServiceProviderInterface
{
    public function register(Container $container): void
    {
        $container->set(ConnectionInterface::class, function() {
            return new PdoConnection(
                dsn: getenv('DB_DSN'),
                username: getenv('DB_USER'),
                password: getenv('DB_PASS')
            );
        });

        $container->set(UserRepository::class, function(Container $c) {
            return new UserRepository($c->get(ConnectionInterface::class));
        });
    }
}

// Register the provider
$provider = new DatabaseServiceProvider();
$provider->register($container);

docs.title: Factory Pattern
docs.text:
$container->set(EmailServiceFactory::class, function() {
    return new class {
        public function create(string $type): EmailServiceInterface {
            return match($type) {
                'smtp' => new SmtpEmailService(),
                'sendgrid' => new SendGridEmailService(),
                default => throw new \InvalidArgumentException("Unknown type: $type")
            };
        }
    };
});

$factory = $container->get(EmailServiceFactory::class);
$emailService = $factory->create('smtp');

docs.title: Contextual Binding
docs.text:
// Different logger for different contexts
$container->set(LoggerInterface::class, function(Container $c) {
    // Default logger
    return new FileLogger('/var/log/app.log');
});

$container->set(AuditService::class, function(Container $c) {
    // Audit service gets a special logger
    return new AuditService(
        new FileLogger('/var/log/audit.log')
    );
});

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Bind interfaces, not implementations in your application code
  2. Use service providers to organize related services
  3. Avoid service locator pattern - inject dependencies via constructor
  4. Register services early in your bootstrap process
  5. Use singletons sparingly - only for stateless or expensive-to-create services

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
<?php
// bootstrap.php

use Tusk\Core\Container\Container;

$container = new Container();

// Configuration
$container->set('config', fn() => require __DIR__ . '/config.php');

// Database
$container->set(ConnectionInterface::class, function(Container $c) {
    $config = $c->get('config');
    return new PdoConnection(
        $config['db']['dsn'],
        $config['db']['user'],
        $config['db']['pass']
    );
});

// Repositories
$container->set(UserRepository::class, function(Container $c) {
    return new UserRepository($c->get(ConnectionInterface::class));
});

// Services
$container->set(AuthService::class, function(Container $c) {
    return new AuthService(
        $c->get(UserRepository::class),
        $c->get(LoggerInterface::class)
    );
});

// Controllers (auto-wired)
// No need to register - container will auto-wire them!

return $container;

docs.title: Application bootstrap
docs.text:
Application projects use Tusk\Foundation\Application as their entry point. The skeleton's bootstrap/app.php composes the app and returns it to the Engine-generated RoadRunner worker:

RoadRunner owns HTTP transport and the PHP worker pool; the Engine supervises that runtime.

use Tusk\Foundation\Application;

return Application::configure(dirname(__DIR__))
    ->withRouting(web: 'routes/web.php')
    ->withProviders(['bootstrap/providers.php'])
    ->create();

Application::configure() returns an ApplicationBuilder. The builder supports routing, providers, controller and job directories, and custom validators before create() returns the application.

docs.title: Application lifecycle
docs.text:
The application exposes these main runtime operations:

  • handle(ServerRequestInterface): ResponseInterface handles one request.
  • runWorker(): void runs the configured RoadRunner worker adapter.
  • start(): void starts the application worker lifecycle.
  • shutdown(): void shuts down the runtime lifecycle.

For ordinary projects, let the Tusk Engine start and supervise RoadRunner; application code should return the configured application from bootstrap/app.php instead of starting a server there. See Engine integration.

docs.title: Low-level runtime kernel
docs.text: Tusk\Runtime\Kernel coordinates Framework lifecycle hooks with a supplied RuntimeAdapterInterface. It is an integration-level runtime component, not the project's HTTP server and not a replacement for the normal application bootstrap. Its public lifecycle methods are start(), run(), stop(), and shutdown().

docs.title: Repository API Reference
docs.text: The Repository pattern provides a clean abstraction for data access.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
use Tusk\Data\Repository\AbstractRepository;
use Tusk\Data\Driver\ConnectionInterface;

class UserRepository extends AbstractRepository
{
    public function __construct(ConnectionInterface $connection)
    {
        parent::__construct($connection);
    }

    public function findAll(): array
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->query('SELECT * FROM users');
        return $stmt->fetchAll(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);
    }

    public function findById(int $id): ?array
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?');
        $stmt->execute([$id]);
        return $stmt->fetch(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC) ?: null;
    }
}

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
public function create(array $data): int
{
    $stmt = $this->connection->prepare(
        'INSERT INTO users (name, email, password) VALUES (?, ?, ?)'
    );

    $stmt->execute([
        $data['name'],
        $data['email'],
        password_hash($data['password'], PASSWORD_BCRYPT)
    ]);

    return (int) $this->connection->lastInsertId();
}

public function findActive(): array

docs.title: Basic Transaction
docs.text:
public function transferFunds(int $fromId, int $toId, float $amount): void
{
    $this->connection->beginTransaction();

    try {
        // Deduct from sender
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare(
            'UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - ? WHERE id = ?'
        );
        $stmt->execute([$amount, $fromId]);

        // Add to receiver
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare(
            'UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + ? WHERE id = ?'
        );
        $stmt->execute([$amount, $toId]);

        $this->connection->commit();
    } catch (\Exception $e) {
        $this->connection->rollback();
        throw $e;
    }
}

docs.title: Dynamic Filters
docs.text:
public function search(array $filters): array
{
    $sql = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE 1=1';
    $params = [];

    if (isset($filters['name'])) {
        $sql .= ' AND name LIKE ?';
        $params[] = '%' . $filters['name'] . '%';
    }

    if (isset($filters['email'])) {
        $sql .= ' AND email = ?';
        $params[] = $filters['email'];
    }

    if (isset($filters['active'])) {
        $sql .= ' AND active = ?';
        $params[] = (int) $filters['active'];
    }

    $stmt = $this->connection->prepare($sql);
    $stmt->execute($params);
    return $stmt->fetchAll(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);
}

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
public function paginate(int $page = 1, int $perPage = 20): array
{
    $offset = ($page - 1) * $perPage;

    // Get total count
    $countStmt = $this->connection->query('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users');
    $total = (int) $countStmt->fetchColumn();

    // Get page data
    $stmt = $this->connection->prepare(
        'SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?'
    );
    $stmt->execute([$perPage, $offset]);
    $data = $stmt->fetchAll(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);

    return [
        'data' => $data,
        'total' => $total,
        'page' => $page,
        'perPage' => $perPage,
        'totalPages' => (int) ceil($total / $perPage)
    ];
}

docs.title: One-to-Many
docs.text:
public function findWithPosts(int $userId): array
{
    // Get user
    $user = $this->findById($userId);
    if (!$user) {
        return null;
    }

    // Get posts
    $stmt = $this->connection->prepare(
        'SELECT * FROM posts WHERE user_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC'
    );
    $stmt->execute([$userId]);
    $user['posts'] = $stmt->fetchAll(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);

    return $user;
}

docs.title: Many-to-Many
docs.text:
public function findWithRoles(int $userId): array
{
    $user = $this->findById($userId);
    if (!$user) {
        return null;
    }

    $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('
        SELECT r.* FROM roles r
        INNER JOIN user_roles ur ON ur.role_id = r.id
        WHERE ur.user_id = ?
    ');
    $stmt->execute([$userId]);
    $user['roles'] = $stmt->fetchAll(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);

    return $user;
}

docs.title: Specification Pattern
docs.text:
interface SpecificationInterface
{
    public function toSql(): string;
    public function getParameters(): array;
}

class ActiveUserSpecification implements SpecificationInterface
{
    public function toSql(): string
    {
        return 'active = ?';
    }

    public function getParameters(): array
    {
        return [1];
    }
}

class UserRepository extends AbstractRepository
{
    public function findBySpecification(SpecificationInterface $spec): array
    {
        $sql = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE ' . $spec->toSql();
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare($sql);
        $stmt->execute($spec->getParameters());
        return $stmt->fetchAll(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);
    }
}

docs.title: Query Object Pattern
docs.text:
class UserQuery
{
    private array $where = [];
    private array $params = [];
    private ?int $limit = null;
    private ?int $offset = null;

    public function whereActive(): self
    {
        $this->where[] = 'active = ?';
        $this->params[] = 1;
        return $this;
    }

    public function whereEmail(string $email): self
    {
        $this->where[] = 'email = ?';
        $this->params[] = $email;
        return $this;
    }

    public function limit(int $limit): self
    {
        $this->limit = $limit;
        return $this;
    }

    public function toSql(): string
    {
        $sql = 'SELECT * FROM users';

        if ($this->where) {
            $sql .= ' WHERE ' . implode(' AND ', $this->where);
        }

        if ($this->limit) {
            $sql .= ' LIMIT ' . $this->limit;
        }

        return $sql;
    }

    public function getParameters(): array
    {
        return $this->params;
    }
}

// Usage
$query = (new UserQuery())
    ->whereActive()
    ->whereEmail('user@example.com')
    ->limit(10);

$stmt = $connection->prepare($query->toSql());
$stmt->execute($query->getParameters());

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
<?php

namespace App\Repository;

use Tusk\Data\Repository\AbstractRepository;
use Tusk\Data\Driver\ConnectionInterface;

class UserRepository extends AbstractRepository
{
    public function __construct(ConnectionInterface $connection)
    {
        parent::__construct($connection);
    }

    public function findAll(): array
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->query('SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY id DESC');
        return $stmt->fetchAll(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC);
    }

    public function findById(int $id): ?array
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?');
        $stmt->execute([$id]);
        return $stmt->fetch(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC) ?: null;
    }

    public function findByEmail(string $email): ?array
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?');
        $stmt->execute([$email]);
        return $stmt->fetch(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC) ?: null;
    }

    public function create(array $data): int
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('
            INSERT INTO users (name, email, password, created_at)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, NOW())
        ');

        $stmt->execute([
            $data['name'],
            $data['email'],
            password_hash($data['password'], PASSWORD_BCRYPT)
        ]);

        return (int) $this->connection->lastInsertId();
    }

    public function update(int $id, array $data): bool
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('
            UPDATE users 
            SET name = ?, email = ?, updated_at = NOW()
            WHERE id = ?
        ');

        return $stmt->execute([
            $data['name'],
            $data['email'],
            $id
        ]);
    }

    public function delete(int $id): bool
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?');
        return $stmt->execute([$id]);
    }
}

docs.title: Router API Reference
docs.text: The Router component handles HTTP request routing and controller resolution.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
use Tusk\Web\Router\Router;
use Tusk\Core\Container\Container;

$container = new Container();
$router = new Router($container);

// Register controllers
$router->registerControllers([
    \App\Controller\UserController::class,
    \App\Controller\ProductController::class,
]);

// Dispatch request
$request = Request::fromGlobals();
$response = $router->dispatch($request);

docs.title: Content Negotiation
docs.text:
#[Route('/users/{id}', methods: ['GET'])]
public function show(Request $request, int $id): Response
{
    $user = $this->userRepo->find($id);

    $accept = $request->getHeader('Accept');

    if (str_contains($accept, 'application/json')) {
        return new Response(200, 
            ['Content-Type' => 'application/json'],
            json_encode($user)
        );
    }

    if (str_contains($accept, 'application/xml')) {
        return new Response(200,
            ['Content-Type' => 'application/xml'],
            $this->toXml($user)
        );
    }

    return new Response(406, [], 'Not Acceptable');
}

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
<?php
// public/index.php

use Tusk\Core\Container\Container;
use Tusk\Web\Router\Router;
use Tusk\Web\Http\Request;

// Bootstrap
$container = require __DIR__ . '/../bootstrap.php';

// Create router
$router = new Router($container);

// Register all controllers
$router->registerControllers([
    \App\Controller\HomeController::class,
    \App\Controller\UserController::class,
    \App\Controller\ProductController::class,
    \App\Controller\OrderController::class,
]);

// Handle request
$request = Request::fromGlobals();

try {
    $response = $router->dispatch($request);
} catch (\Tusk\Web\Exception\RouteNotFoundException $e) {
    $response = new Response(404, [], 'Not Found');
} catch (\Tusk\Web\Exception\MethodNotAllowedException $e) {
    $response = new Response(405, ['Allow' => implode(', ', $e->getAllowedMethods())]);
} catch (\Throwable $e) {
    error_log($e->getMessage());
    $response = new Response(500, [], 'Internal Server Error');
}

// Send response
$response->send();

docs.title: Core (Dependency Injection)
docs.text: The tusk-core component provides the foundation for dependency management.

docs.title: Container
docs.text: The Container class is a simple, attribute-based DI container.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
use Tusk\Core\Container\Container;

$container = new Container();

// Register a service
$container->set(DatabaseConnection::class, function() {
    return new DatabaseConnection('mysql:host=localhost');
});

// Resolve a service
$db = $container->get(DatabaseConnection::class);

docs.title: Auto-Wiring
docs.text:
The container can automatically resolve constructor dependencies:

class UserService
{
    public function __construct(
        private UserRepository $repo,
        private Logger $logger
    ) {}
}

// Container will automatically inject dependencies
$service = $container->get(UserService::class);

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text:
Core interfaces that define framework behavior:

  • ContainerInterface - DI container contract
  • KernelInterface - Application kernel contract
  • ServiceProviderInterface - Service registration

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
PHP 8 attributes for declarative configuration:

  • #[Service] - Mark a class as a service
  • #[Singleton] - Register as singleton
  • #[Inject] - Explicit dependency injection

docs.title: Example: Service Provider
docs.text:
use Tusk\Core\Attribute\Service;

#[Service]
class AppServiceProvider
{
    public function register(Container $container): void
    {
        $container->set(LoggerInterface::class, function() {
            return new FileLogger('/var/log/app.log');
        });
    }
}

docs.title: Data (Repository)
docs.text: The tusk-data component provides database abstraction and repository pattern.

docs.title: PdoConnection
docs.text:
Resilient PDO wrapper with automatic reconnection:

use Tusk\Data\Driver\Pdo\PdoConnection;

$db = new PdoConnection('mysql:host=localhost;dbname=app', 'user', 'pass');

docs.title: AbstractRepository
docs.text:
Base class for clean data access:

use Tusk\Data\Repository\AbstractRepository;

class UserRepository extends AbstractRepository
{
    public function findByEmail(string $email): ?array
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?');
        $stmt->execute([$email]);
        return $stmt->fetch(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC) ?: null;
    }
}

docs.text:

try {
    // ... operations
    $db->commit();
} catch (\Exception $e) {
    $db->rollback();
}

Full documentation coming soon.

docs.title: Tusk Engine Control Plane
docs.text:
The Tusk Engine is a Go control plane for a Tusk application running on RoadRunner. It validates project/runtime configuration, generates the RoadRunner configuration at startup, starts and supervises the RoadRunner process, and exposes operational diagnostics.

graph TD
    CLI["Tusk CLI / Engine"] -->|configure and supervise| RR["RoadRunner"]
    Client["HTTP client"] -->|HTTP| RR
    RR -->|dispatches requests| PHP["PHP workers"]
    PHP --> App["Tusk Framework application"]

RoadRunner is the HTTP data plane and owns the PHP worker pool, request dispatch, recycling, and worker shutdown. The Engine does not duplicate these responsibilities or proxy application traffic.

docs.title: Project files
docs.text:
• tusk.json contains Engine/platform settings.
  • composer.json and its lockfile contain PHP dependencies and scripts.
  • bootstrap/app.php composes the Framework application.
  • .tusk/runtime/ contains Engine-generated runtime state; generated files are not application source and should not be committed.

Use tusk doctor to diagnose the project and tusk start to generate the runtime configuration and start RoadRunner. Runtime configuration is generated during startup; the current application workflow has no separate compile or package-artifact phase.

docs.title: Micro (Microservices)
docs.text: The tusk-micro component provides utilities for cloud-native microservices.

docs.title: Health Checks
docs.text:
Standard Kubernetes-style health endpoints:

use Tusk\Micro\Health\HealthCheckRegistry;
use Tusk\Micro\Controller\HealthController;

$registry = new HealthCheckRegistry();
$registry->register(new DatabaseCheck());

$controller = new HealthController($registry);

Endpoints: - /health/live - Liveness probe (always UP) - /health/ready - Readiness probe (checks registry)

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Prometheus-compatible metrics:

use Tusk\Micro\Metric\Prometheus;

$metrics = new Prometheus();
$metrics->counter('requests_total')->inc();

docs.title: RPC Interfaces
docs.text:
Define gRPC-style service contracts:

use Tusk\Micro\Rpc\RpcServiceInterface;

interface UserServiceInterface extends RpcServiceInterface
{
    public function getUser(int $id): User;
}

Full documentation coming soon.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Tusk separates application behavior from process/runtime management.

HTTP client
    ↓
RoadRunner — HTTP transport and PHP worker lifecycle
    ↓
PHP worker — Tusk Framework application
                  ├─ bootstrap and dependency injection
                  ├─ routing and middleware
                  └─ application services and persistence

Tusk Engine — validates configuration and supervises RoadRunner

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Tusk Framework: application bootstrap, dependency injection, routing, request handling, validation, and application-level components.
  • Tusk Engine: CLI, project diagnostics, generated runtime configuration, process supervision, and operational health/metrics.
  • RoadRunner: owns HTTP transport and PHP worker processes, including worker pooling and recycling.
  • Composer: package resolution, lockfile, autoloading, and PHP scripts.

The Engine manages the runtime but is not in the public request path. This avoids implementing a second HTTP server, worker pool, or request transport. See Engine integration for the lifecycle.

docs.title: Runtime Lifecycle
docs.text: The Engine manages RoadRunner's lifecycle; it does not implement a separate PHP request loop.

docs.title: Startup
docs.text:
1. tusk doctor reports project bootstrap and toolchain diagnostics.
  2. tusk start validates bootstrap/app.php and project configuration.
  3. The Engine generates RoadRunner configuration and private worker state under .tusk/runtime/.
  4. The Engine starts RoadRunner and monitors runtime readiness and process health.

docs.title: Request handling
docs.text: RoadRunner accepts HTTP traffic and dispatches requests to persistent PHP workers. Each worker loads the Composer autoloader and application bootstrap; the Framework handles each request. RoadRunner owns worker pooling, recycling, and worker process shutdown. Application code should treat workers as long-lived and avoid leaking request-specific state.

docs.title: Shutdown and diagnostics
docs.text:
The Engine supervises RoadRunner and coordinates shutdown when it receives a termination signal. tusk doctor diagnoses the local project/toolchain; Engine control and metrics endpoints, when enabled, report runtime operations.

The RoadRunner configuration is generated as part of tusk start.

docs.title: Web and Routing
docs.text:
The Framework's web layer matches routes, resolves controllers, applies middleware, and handles PSR-7 server requests. RoadRunner provides the HTTP listener and dispatches requests to the PHP worker; Tusk\Web\HttpKernel is an application request handler, not a socket-based HTTP server.

RoadRunner owns the HTTP listener and PHP worker pool.

docs.title: Attribute routes
docs.text:
The router discovers controller methods marked with #[Route]. A controller can return a PSR-7 response; arrays and objects are encoded as JSON by the HTTP kernel.

use Tusk\Web\Attribute\Route;

final class StatusController
{
    #[Route('/status', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function show(): array
    {
        return ['status' => 'ok'];
    }
}

The standard application skeleton registers controllers from app/Controller and starts them through the Framework bootstrap and RoadRunner runtime. See Your First App for a runnable example.

docs.title: Your First App
docs.text:
The project skeleton includes a small typed product API at /api/products. It demonstrates JSON input validation and returning an HTTP response through the Framework and RoadRunner.

Start the application from its project directory:

tusk doctor
tusk start

In another terminal, create a product:

curl -i \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Notebook","sku":"NOTE-1"}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/products

The example stores products in process memory. It is intended to demonstrate the request path, not persistence: workers do not share their in-memory state, and that state is lost when a worker restarts. Use a database-backed repository for application data that must persist or be shared across workers.

The application bootstrap is bootstrap/app.php; routes and controllers live in the application source. See the Framework API guides when extending the example.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• PHP 8.2 or newer with the extensions required by your application.
  • Composer 2 for creating the project and installing PHP dependencies.
  • The Tusk Engine binary on your PATH as tusk.
  • RoadRunner (rr) available to the Engine at runtime.

tusk doctor diagnoses the selected tools but does not install them. Install and manage PHP and RoadRunner using your platform's package/release workflow, or follow the Engine's explicit toolchain-provisioning documentation when a verified catalog is configured.

docs.title: Install the Engine
docs.text: Download the archive for your operating system and architecture from the Tusk Engine releases, then put the tusk executable on your PATH. Follow the release asset's included instructions for your platform.

docs.title: Create an application
docs.text:
composer create-project tusk-framework/app catalog
cd catalog

Before starting the server, verify that the project bootstrap and required tools are available:

tusk doctor

Continue to the Quick Start to run the app.

docs.title: Contributing to the Framework
docs.text: To work on the Framework source itself, clone tusk-framework/tusk-framework and follow its CONTRIBUTING.md. Cloning the Framework is not required to create an application.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Create a project, check its prerequisites, and start it under RoadRunner.

docs.title: Create the project
docs.text:
composer create-project tusk-framework/app catalog
cd catalog

Composer creates the application and installs its dependencies. The app entry point is bootstrap/app.php; you do not need to create a root worker.php.

docs.title: Diagnose and start
docs.text:
tusk doctor
tusk start

tusk doctor reports the project and toolchain status. tusk start validates the application bootstrap, generates the RoadRunner configuration, and supervises RoadRunner. RoadRunner listens for HTTP requests and manages the PHP workers. The default application address is http://127.0.0.1:8080 unless changed in tusk.json.

Try the sample endpoint with Your First App, or read about CLI commands.

docs.title: Authentication Guide
docs.text: Implement authentication and authorization in your Tusk applications.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: composer require firebase/php-jwt

docs.title: JWT Service
docs.text:
<?php

namespace App\Service;

use Firebase\JWT\JWT;
use Firebase\JWT\Key;

class JwtService
{
    private string $secret;
    private string $algorithm = 'HS256';

    public function __construct(string $secret)
    {
        $this->secret = $secret;
    }

    public function encode(array $payload): string
    {
        $payload['iat'] = time();
        $payload['exp'] = time() + (60 * 60 * 24); // 24 hours

        return JWT::encode($payload, $this->secret, $this->algorithm);
    }

    public function decode(string $token): object
    {
        return JWT::decode($token, new Key($this->secret, $this->algorithm));
    }

    public function verify(string $token): bool
    {
        try {
            $this->decode($token);
            return true;
        } catch (\Exception $e) {
            return false;
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Auth Service
docs.text:
<?php

namespace App\Service;

use App\Repository\UserRepository;

class AuthService
{
    public function __construct(
        private UserRepository $userRepo,
        private JwtService $jwt
    ) {}

    public function login(string $email, string $password): ?string
    {
        $user = $this->userRepo->findByEmail($email);

        if (!$user || !password_verify($password, $user['password'])) {
            return null;
        }

        return $this->jwt->encode([
            'user_id' => $user['id'],
            'email' => $user['email'],
        ]);
    }

    public function verify(string $token): ?array
    {
        try {
            $payload = $this->jwt->decode($token);
            return $this->userRepo->findById($payload->user_id);
        } catch (\Exception $e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    public function register(array $data): int
    {
        $data['password'] = password_hash($data['password'], PASSWORD_BCRYPT);
        return $this->userRepo->create($data);
    }
}

docs.title: Auth Controller
docs.text:
<?php

namespace App\Controller;

use Tusk\Web\Attribute\Route;
use Tusk\Web\Http\Request;
use Tusk\Web\Http\Response;
use App\Service\AuthService;

class AuthController
{
    public function __construct(
        private AuthService $auth
    ) {}

    #[Route('/auth/register', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function register(Request $request): Response
    {
        $data = json_decode($request->getBody(), true);

        // Validate
        if (!isset($data['email'], $data['password'], $data['name'])) {
            return new Response(400, [], json_encode([
                'error' => 'Missing required fields'
            ]));
        }

        // Register user
        try {
            $userId = $this->auth->register($data);

            return new Response(201, [], json_encode([
                'id' => $userId,
                'message' => 'User registered successfully'
            ]));
        } catch (\Exception $e) {
            return new Response(500, [], json_encode([
                'error' => 'Registration failed'
            ]));
        }
    }

    #[Route('/auth/login', methods: ['POST'])]
    public function login(Request $request): Response
    {
        $data = json_decode($request->getBody(), true);

        if (!isset($data['email'], $data['password'])) {
            return new Response(400, [], json_encode([
                'error' => 'Email and password required'
            ]));
        }

        $token = $this->auth->login($data['email'], $data['password']);

        if (!$token) {
            return new Response(401, [], json_encode([
                'error' => 'Invalid credentials'
            ]));
        }

        return new Response(200, [], json_encode([
            'token' => $token
        ]));
    }

    #[Route('/auth/me', methods: ['GET'])]
    public function me(Request $request): Response
    {
        $authHeader = $request->getHeader('Authorization');

        if (!$authHeader || !str_starts_with($authHeader, 'Bearer ')) {
            return new Response(401, [], json_encode([
                'error' => 'Unauthorized'
            ]));
        }

        $token = substr($authHeader, 7);
        $user = $this->auth->verify($token);

        if (!$user) {
            return new Response(401, [], json_encode([
                'error' => 'Invalid token'
            ]));
        }

        // Remove sensitive data
        unset($user['password']);

        return new Response(200, [], json_encode($user));
    }
}

docs.title: Middleware (Future Feature)
docs.text:
<?php

namespace App\Middleware;

use Tusk\Web\Http\Request;
use Tusk\Web\Http\Response;
use App\Service\AuthService;

class AuthMiddleware
{
    public function __construct(
        private AuthService $auth
    ) {}

    public function handle(Request $request, callable $next): Response
    {
        $authHeader = $request->getHeader('Authorization');

        if (!$authHeader || !str_starts_with($authHeader, 'Bearer ')) {
            return new Response(401, [], json_encode([
                'error' => 'Unauthorized'
            ]));
        }

        $token = substr($authHeader, 7);
        $user = $this->auth->verify($token);

        if (!$user) {
            return new Response(401, [], json_encode([
                'error' => 'Invalid token'
            ]));
        }

        // Attach user to request
        $request->setAttribute('user', $user);

        return $next($request);
    }
}

docs.title: Manual Check
docs.text:
#[Route('/users/{id}', methods: ['PUT'])]
public function update(Request $request, int $id): Response
{
    // Get authenticated user
    $authHeader = $request->getHeader('Authorization');
    if (!$authHeader) {
        return new Response(401, [], json_encode(['error' => 'Unauthorized']));
    }

    $token = substr($authHeader, 7);
    $user = $this->auth->verify($token);

    if (!$user) {
        return new Response(401, [], json_encode(['error' => 'Invalid token']));
    }

    // Check authorization
    if ($user['id'] !== $id && !$user['is_admin']) {
        return new Response(403, [], json_encode(['error' => 'Forbidden']));
    }

    // Update user
    $data = json_decode($request->getBody(), true);
    $this->userRepo->update($id, $data);

    return new Response(200, [], json_encode(['message' => 'Updated']));
}

docs.title: User Roles
docs.text:
class UserRepository extends AbstractRepository
{
    public function findWithRoles(int $userId): array
    {
        $user = $this->findById($userId);

        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('
            SELECT r.name FROM roles r
            INNER JOIN user_roles ur ON ur.role_id = r.id
            WHERE ur.user_id = ?
        ');
        $stmt->execute([$userId]);

        $user['roles'] = array_column($stmt->fetchAll(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC), 'name');

        return $user;
    }

    public function hasRole(int $userId, string $role): bool
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('
            SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_roles ur
            INNER JOIN roles r ON r.id = ur.role_id
            WHERE ur.user_id = ? AND r.name = ?
        ');
        $stmt->execute([$userId, $role]);

        return (int) $stmt->fetchColumn() > 0;
    }
}

docs.title: Authorization Helper
docs.text:
class AuthorizationService
{
    public function __construct(
        private UserRepository $userRepo
    ) {}

    public function can(int $userId, string $permission): bool
    {
        $stmt = $this->connection->prepare('
            SELECT COUNT(*) FROM permissions p
            INNER JOIN role_permissions rp ON rp.permission_id = p.id
            INNER JOIN user_roles ur ON ur.role_id = rp.role_id
            WHERE ur.user_id = ? AND p.name = ?
        ');
        $stmt->execute([$userId, $permission]);

        return (int) $stmt->fetchColumn() > 0;
    }
}

docs.title: Session Service
docs.text:
class SessionService
{
    public function start(): void
    {
        if (session_status() === PHP_SESSION_NONE) {
            session_start();
        }
    }

    public function set(string $key, mixed $value): void
    {
        $_SESSION[$key] = $value;
    }

    public function get(string $key, mixed $default = null): mixed
    {
        return $_SESSION[$key] ?? $default;
    }

    public function has(string $key): bool
    {
        return isset($_SESSION[$key]);
    }

    public function remove(string $key): void
    {
        unset($_SESSION[$key]);
    }

    public function destroy(): void
    {
        session_destroy();
    }
}

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
<?php
// Register services in bootstrap.php

$container->set(JwtService::class, function() {
    return new JwtService(getenv('JWT_SECRET'));
});

$container->set(AuthService::class, function(Container $c) {
    return new AuthService(
        $c->get(UserRepository::class),
        $c->get(JwtService::class)
    );
});

// Usage in client
// POST /auth/register
{
    "name": "Alice",
    "email": "alice@example.com",
    "password": "secret123"
}

// POST /auth/login
{
    "email": "alice@example.com",
    "password": "secret123"
}
// Response: { "token": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGc..." }

// GET /auth/me
// Headers: Authorization: Bearer eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGc...
// Response: { "id": 1, "name": "Alice", "email": "alice@example.com" }

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text: Run the tusk CLI from the application directory. Use tusk --help in the installed Engine version for the complete command list.

docs.title: Diagnose the project
docs.text:
tusk doctor
tusk doctor --json

The diagnostic report helps identify the application bootstrap and toolchain executables used by the project. It does not install tools or change the machine.

docs.title: Start the application
docs.text:
tusk start

The Engine validates the application bootstrap, generates RoadRunner's configuration, and supervises the runtime. tusk dev is an alias for tusk start.

docs.title: Configure the project
docs.text:
tusk init initializes Engine configuration (tusk.json) in an existing project; it does not scaffold a PHP application. To create a new app, use Composer's create-project command with tusk-framework/app.

The Engine reads platform settings from tusk.json. Composer owns package dependencies, the lockfile, and Composer scripts in composer.json.

docs.title: Toolchain commands
docs.text:
tusk toolchain list
tusk toolchain pin php@8.3

Toolchain setup is explicit. Read the Engine's offline documentation before provisioning managed tools.

docs.title: Offline documentation
docs.text:
tusk docs
tusk docs runtime

The installed Engine includes version-matched documentation, so these pages remain available without opening the website.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Deploy the application, PHP runtime, Composer dependencies, Tusk Engine, and RoadRunner as explicit parts of your runtime environment. The Engine supervises RoadRunner; RoadRunner owns the public HTTP listener and PHP workers.

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
1. Install a supported PHP version and the extensions required by your app.
  2. Commit the application's composer.lock, then install its locked dependencies, for example with composer install --no-dev --prefer-dist --no-interaction --optimize-autoloader.
  3. Install the Tusk Engine and RoadRunner versions selected for the deployment.
  4. Provide production configuration and secrets through your platform's secret management; do not commit credentials.
  5. Run tusk doctor as a deployment check, then start the app with tusk start.
  6. Configure the platform's TLS termination, health checks, logging, and restart policy. Expose only the intended public listener.

The Engine generates RoadRunner configuration at startup from the project configuration. The application is served from its Composer project; no separate application artifact is produced by the current runtime workflow.

docs.title: Reverse proxy and TLS
docs.text: When TLS termination or edge routing is required, place the deployment's existing load balancer or reverse proxy in front of RoadRunner. This is an infrastructure choice; the Engine does not proxy HTTP traffic.

docs.title: Long-lived workers
docs.text: RoadRunner workers handle multiple requests over their lifetime. Avoid keeping request-specific mutable state in long-lived services. Use a database or shared cache for state shared between workers and instances, and follow the Framework's request-scope lifecycle when adding application services.

docs.title: Engine and Framework Integration
docs.text: The Engine and Framework have separate responsibilities. The Framework composes and handles the PHP application; the Engine validates the project, generates RoadRunner configuration, and supervises the runtime; RoadRunner serves HTTP and manages PHP workers.

docs.title: Request lifecycle
docs.text:
1. A client sends an HTTP request to RoadRunner.
  2. RoadRunner dispatches the request to an available PHP worker.
  3. The worker loads bootstrap/app.php and handles requests through the Tusk Framework application lifecycle.
  4. RoadRunner returns the application's response to the client.

The PHP application is long-lived within each worker, so its bootstrap is not repeated for every request. Request-specific state must not leak across requests; use the Framework's request lifecycle and shared infrastructure for persistent data.

docs.title: Start the managed runtime
docs.text:
From the project root:

tusk doctor
tusk start

The Engine checks the bootstrap and toolchain, generates private runtime state under .tusk/runtime/, and starts RoadRunner. Do not edit or commit the generated worker. The application entry point remains bootstrap/app.php; there is no root-level worker.php contract.

docs.title: Responsibility boundary
docs.text:
Concern Owner Project bootstrap, routes, middleware, request handling Tusk Framework Project diagnostics, runtime configuration, process supervision Tusk Engine HTTP transport, PHP workers, worker pool and recycling RoadRunner

The default request path is direct:

client → RoadRunner → PHP worker → Tusk Framework
                    ↑
             supervised by Engine

RoadRunner owns the HTTP transport and PHP worker pool. The Engine is not an HTTP proxy and does not implement a second worker pool or an application-level request protocol.

docs.title: Testing Guide
docs.text: Learn how to test your Tusk applications effectively.

docs.title: Testing Controllers
docs.text:
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
use Tusk\Web\Http\Request;
use App\Controller\UserController;

class UserControllerTest extends TestCase
{
    private UserController $controller;
    private UserRepository $mockRepo;

    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        $this->mockRepo = $this->createMock(UserRepository::class);
        $this->controller = new UserController($this->mockRepo);
    }

    public function testListUsers(): void
    {
        // Arrange
        $this->mockRepo
            ->expects($this->once())
            ->method('findAll')
            ->willReturn([
                ['id' => 1, 'name' => 'Alice'],
                ['id' => 2, 'name' => 'Bob'],
            ]);

        $request = new Request('GET', '/users', [], [], '');

        // Act
        $response = $this->controller->list($request);

        // Assert
        $this->assertEquals(200, $response->getStatusCode());
        $data = json_decode($response->getBody(), true);
        $this->assertCount(2, $data);
    }

    public function testShowUser(): void
    {
        // Arrange
        $this->mockRepo
            ->expects($this->once())
            ->method('findById')
            ->with(1)
            ->willReturn(['id' => 1, 'name' => 'Alice']);

        $request = new Request('GET', '/users/1', [], [], '');

        // Act
        $response = $this->controller->show($request, 1);

        // Assert
        $this->assertEquals(200, $response->getStatusCode());
    }
}

docs.title: Testing Repositories
docs.text:
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
use Tusk\Data\Driver\ConnectionInterface;
use App\Repository\UserRepository;

class UserRepositoryTest extends TestCase
{
    private UserRepository $repo;
    private ConnectionInterface $mockConnection;

    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        $this->mockConnection = $this->createMock(ConnectionInterface::class);
        $this->repo = new UserRepository($this->mockConnection);
    }

    public function testFindById(): void
    {
        // Arrange
        $mockStmt = $this->createMock(\PDOStatement::class);
        $mockStmt->expects($this->once())
            ->method('execute')
            ->with([1]);
        $mockStmt->expects($this->once())
            ->method('fetch')
            ->willReturn(['id' => 1, 'name' => 'Alice']);

        $this->mockConnection
            ->expects($this->once())
            ->method('prepare')
            ->with('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?')
            ->willReturn($mockStmt);

        // Act
        $user = $this->repo->findById(1);

        // Assert
        $this->assertEquals(1, $user['id']);
        $this->assertEquals('Alice', $user['name']);
    }
}

docs.title: Database Testing
docs.text:
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
use Tusk\Data\Driver\Pdo\PdoConnection;
use App\Repository\UserRepository;

class UserRepositoryIntegrationTest extends TestCase
{
    private PdoConnection $connection;
    private UserRepository $repo;

    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        // Use SQLite in-memory database for testing
        $this->connection = new PdoConnection('sqlite::memory:');

        // Create schema
        $this->connection->exec('
            CREATE TABLE users (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                name TEXT NOT NULL,
                email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL
            )
        ');

        $this->repo = new UserRepository($this->connection);
    }

    public function testCreateAndFind(): void
    {
        // Create user
        $id = $this->repo->create([
            'name' => 'Alice',
            'email' => 'alice@example.com'
        ]);

        // Find user
        $user = $this->repo->findById($id);

        $this->assertEquals('Alice', $user['name']);
        $this->assertEquals('alice@example.com', $user['email']);
    }

    public function testUpdate(): void
    {
        $id = $this->repo->create([
            'name' => 'Alice',
            'email' => 'alice@example.com'
        ]);

        $this->repo->update($id, [
            'name' => 'Alice Smith',
            'email' => 'alice.smith@example.com'
        ]);

        $user = $this->repo->findById($id);
        $this->assertEquals('Alice Smith', $user['name']);
    }
}

docs.title: Testing Routes

use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
use Tusk\Web\Router\Router;
use Tusk\Web\Http\Request;
use Tusk\Core\Container\Container;

class RouterTest extends TestCase

    protected function setUp(): void

        $container = new Container();
        $this->router = new Router($container);
        $this->router->registerControllers([
            \App\Controller\UserController::class,
        ]);

    public function testGetUsers(): void
    {
        $request = new Request('GET', '/users', [], [], '');
        $response = $this->router->dispatch($request);

        $this->assertEquals(200, $response->getStatusCode());
    }

    public function testPostUser(): void
    {
        $request = new Request('POST', '/users', 
            ['Content-Type' => 'application/json'],
            [],
            json_encode(['name' => 'Alice', 'email' => 'alice@example.com'])
        );

        $response = $this->router->dispatch($request);

        $this->assertEquals(201, $response->getStatusCode());
    }

    public function test404NotFound(): void
    {
        $this->expectException(\Tusk\Web\Exception\RouteNotFoundException::class);

        $request = new Request('GET', '/nonexistent', [], [], '');
        $this->router->dispatch($request);
    }
}

docs.text:

    {
        $users = [
            ['name' => 'Alice', 'email' => 'alice@example.com'],
            ['name' => 'Bob', 'email' => 'bob@example.com'],
            ['name' => 'Charlie', 'email' => 'charlie@example.com'],
        ];

        $stmt = $connection->prepare('
            INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)
        ');

        foreach ($users as $user) {
            $stmt->execute([$user['name'], $user['email']]);
        }
    }
}

// Usage in tests
protected function setUp(): void
{
    parent::setUp();
    DatabaseFixtures::loadUsers($this->connection);
}

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:

./vendor/bin/phpunit

# Run specific suite

# Run with coverage
./vendor/bin/phpunit --coverage-html coverage/

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Test Isolation - Each test should be independent
  2. Mock External Dependencies - Don't hit real databases/APIs in unit tests
  3. Use In-Memory Databases - SQLite for integration tests
  4. Descriptive Test Names - testCreateUserWithValidData()
  5. Arrange-Act-Assert - Structure tests clearly
  6. Test Edge Cases - Not just happy paths
  7. Keep Tests Fast - Unit tests should run in milliseconds

docs.title: Tusk Application Golden Path Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Keep each repository change in its own PR/worktree and verify every acceptance criterion before reporting completion.

Goal: Deliver and verify one public, stable path from a clean Composer install to a Tusk application served by RoadRunner, consistently across the App skeleton, Engine, and Docs.

Architecture: Composer creates the project; the Framework owns application bootstrap and request handling; the Engine validates/configures and supervises RoadRunner; RoadRunner owns HTTP transport and PHP workers. No Engine proxy or second worker pool is introduced. Framework's separately reviewed breaking cleanup and major release is a prerequisite to publishing the App skeleton against that API.

Tech Stack: PHP 8.2+, Composer/Packagist, Go CLI, RoadRunner, PowerShell smoke harness (Linux CI), MkDocs Material.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-application-golden-path-design.md (merged in Docs PR #3).

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Update each repository's local main from origin/main and verify its tracked baseline before creating implementation branches/worktrees.
  • Never use codex/ in branch names. Use conventional repository prefixes and lowercase kebab-case.
  • Preserve existing user worktrees and untracked files; all repository work is delivered through separate PRs.
  • Do not begin the Framework mock/discovery removal from this plan. Framework PR #61 is a separate draft design-review gate; only after its spec is approved should that work receive its own implementation plan and approval. Publish the resulting Framework major before changing/registering the App package.
  • Confirm the actual published Framework tag before setting the App constraint (expected ^1.0.0, not an assumption).
  • Never use a local path repository or dev-* Framework dependency to prove the public consumer path.
  • Keep tuskpress an example, not a product requirement. Do not add a gateway, native server, service mesh, duplicate worker pool, or unrelated app features.
  • Do not commit Packagist credentials or webhook secrets. If account-level package registration is unavailable, stop at the external prerequisite and report it.
  • Issue #9 is closed only after all public-package/runtime/docs evidence is recorded.

docs.title: Dependency Order
docs.text:
Framework PR #61 spec review → separately planned implementation → breaking major release
                                                        ↓
                                      App identity + Packagist publication
                                      ↙                       ↘
                         Engine public-consumer smoke       Docs rewrite/build
                                      ↘                       ↙
                                  clean end-to-end proof → Framework issue #9

Docs may be implemented independently after this plan is approved. Engine harness work can be prepared independently, but its public-package run is gated on App registration and stable indexing. Framework PR #61 must not be treated as implementation approval merely because its checks are green.

docs.title: PR 1 — App package identity and public installation
docs.text: Repository: tusk-app Branch: chore/packagist-app-identity Prerequisite: Framework breaking cleanup merged and its compatible stable major is available from Packagist.

docs.title: Files / behavior
docs.text:
• composer.json: set package name to tusk-framework/app; retain type: project; require the actually published compatible stable Framework major.
  • README.md: canonical composer create-project tusk-framework/app <directory> flow, then tusk doctor and tusk start; explain the sample /api/products route is in-memory and not persistence. Do not include tusk build.
  • Existing manifest/package identity tests (locate current test path before editing): assert the exact vendor/package name and project type; reject old tusk/app identity and local/dev dependencies.
  • Any metadata or install instructions in the skeleton must use the Composer package name while keeping GitHub repository slug tusk-framework/tusk-app.

docs.title: TDD / verification
docs.text:
1. Add/update manifest tests first; run the focused test and confirm it fails on the old name/constraint.
  2. Change manifest and README; run the focused test and full App test suite.
  3. Run composer validate --strict and composer install --no-interaction --prefer-dist from a clean temporary copy.
  4. Verify the installed composer.lock resolves a stable Framework tag satisfying the new constraint, with no path repository and no dev-* package version.
  5. Verify CI's supported PHP matrix (currently 8.2–8.5) and open a PR with the standard summary, rationale, verification, and release-impact sections.

docs.title: Packagist release gate (external account action)
docs.text:
1. Register tusk-framework/app from the tusk-framework/tusk-app GitHub repository only after the manifest points at the published Framework major.
  2. Configure Packagist's GitHub auto-update hook using Packagist/GitHub UI or authorized tooling; keep credentials out of source and logs.
  3. Verify a package metadata refresh and then run composer create-project tusk-framework/app <empty-temp-directory> --no-interaction --prefer-dist from outside all Tusk checkouts.
  4. Confirm package metadata/version and installed Framework version from Composer output/lockfile. A webhook HTTP 2xx alone is insufficient proof of indexing.

docs.title: PR 2 — Docs canonical getting-started path
docs.text: Repository: tusk-docs Branch: docs/published-app-golden-path

docs.title: Files / behavior
docs.text:
Rewrite only pages that contradict the merged spec/current CLI; inspect each page before editing:

  • docs/index.md
  • docs/getting-started/installation.md
  • docs/getting-started/quickstart.md
  • docs/getting-started/first-app.md
  • docs/guides/cli-usage.md
  • docs/guides/deployment.md
  • docs/guides/engine-integration.md
  • docs/architecture/engine.md
  • docs/architecture/overview.md
  • docs/architecture/runtime.md
  • docs/architecture/web.md (currently advertises a removed PHP socket server).
  • docs/api/kernel.md (currently documents removed Kernel methods and a removed HTTP server).
  • mkdocs.yml navigation labels where they describe removed Native Engine behavior.

Present one verified path: install Engine prerequisites, composer create-project tusk-framework/app <directory>, cd <directory>, tusk doctor, tusk start, then request the sample endpoint. Explain which component owns each action; distinguish Engine lifecycle supervision from RoadRunner's HTTP/worker ownership; state the in-memory sample limitation. Do not document tusk build: the CLI has no such built-in command, configuration generation happens during tusk start, and no build artifact is currently defined. Revisit only alongside a concrete build/optimization design. Remove active user-doc claims about Engine-owned request pools/IPC, NDJSON, root worker.php, native HTTP transport, or tusk init <name> scaffolding. Preserve unrelated guides only after verifying their examples against current code.

docs.title: TDD / verification
docs.text:
1. Add tests/test_golden_path_docs.py before the rewrite. Assert the public create-project command plus tusk doctor and tusk start; assert active onboarding pages do not show an unsupported tusk build command; verify RoadRunner owns HTTP/workers; reject obsolete runtime claims in active pages. Keep historical specs/archives outside the active-page scan.
  2. Rewrite pages/navigation; run that focused check and search active docs for worker.php, NDJSON, tusk init <name>, and claims that Engine owns HTTP/worker pools. Review each hit rather than blindly deleting valid API references.
  3. Install dependencies using the repository's documented MkDocs setup and run mkdocs build --strict.
  4. Add .github/workflows/validate.yml to install MkDocs and its Material theme, run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v, and run mkdocs build --strict on pull requests and pushes to main; use a supported Python version and read-only repository permissions. Verify workflow syntax and commands before opening the PR.
  5. Open the PR with rendered navigation/page list and exact build evidence. If package installation/network is unavailable, do not claim strict-build success; leave that check pending and report the environmental blocker.

docs.title: PR 3 — Engine clean public-consumer smoke
docs.text: Repository: tusk-engine Branch: test/public-app-golden-path Prerequisite for public run: App package registered and composer create-project succeeds from Packagist.

docs.title: Files / behavior
docs.text:
• Add a dedicated test/skeleton/public-app.ps1 (or equivalent isolated test harness) and focused Go contract tests for its invocation/acceptance behavior where practical.
  • Extend .github/workflows/test.yml to run this consumer smoke in addition to, not instead of, the existing comprehensive generated-skeleton/local-Framework smoke.
  • Use a fresh temporary directory, public composer create-project, the built Engine binary, CI's actual RoadRunner binary, and no local Framework checkout/path repository/dev package.
  • Exercise the documented sequence tusk doctor, tusk start; verify startup generates the RoadRunner configuration and use a bounded readiness loop to request POST /api/products, asserting HTTP 201 and the expected response shape. Verify Engine exits non-zero on failed stages, preserve useful logs, and always terminate/reap Engine, RoadRunner, and PHP children on success/failure/timeout.
  • Use dynamically allocated loopback ports where supported; avoid races from probe-then-bind if the CLI can accept a port through generated config. Confirm actual generated config and CLI behavior before choosing the port injection mechanism.
  • Keep existing test/skeleton/smoke.ps1 semantics and its local Framework path override intact; this new smoke is separate specifically to cover published-consumer behavior.

docs.title: TDD / verification
docs.text:
1. Add harness contract tests first for the command sequence, no local/path/dev dependency, non-zero failures, bounded startup, HTTP assertion, and cleanup path; demonstrate failure before implementation.
  2. Implement the isolated script and workflow invocation. Exercise on Linux with PHP, Composer, Go, RoadRunner, and a real published App package.
  3. Run go test ./..., go vet ./..., existing skeleton smoke, and the new public smoke. Confirm the new test runs in CI rather than silently returning a skipped success when a required public prerequisite is absent.
  4. Capture Engine/RoadRunner logs on failure and verify the harness cleans all child processes. Keep credentials/secrets out of logs and test artifacts.
  5. Open a separate PR with explicit public package/version and smoke evidence.

docs.title: Final acceptance and issue #9
docs.text:
After the App package is indexed and all three PRs are merged:

  1. From an empty temporary directory not nested under any repository, run the exact documented composer create-project tusk-framework/app ... command.
  2. Verify the installed Framework is a stable published major and run the skeleton's test suite/manifest validation.
  3. Run tusk doctor, tusk start; send the documented HTTP request and assert the response through RoadRunner.
  4. Run mkdocs build --strict and the active-doc obsolete-claim scan.
  5. Record exact versions, commands/results, and links to the App/Engine/Docs PRs on Framework issue #9; close it only if every acceptance criterion passes. If Packagist account/indexing is blocked, keep #9 open and report precisely which external step remains.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• Does the public Composer package use exactly tusk-framework/app, retain type: project, and resolve a stable compatible Framework release?
  • Does any proof accidentally depend on a local checkout, path repository, or dev-* release?
  • Does documentation assign HTTP transport and PHP worker lifecycle to RoadRunner, not Engine?
  • Are sample state limitations clear, without promoting TuskPress or claiming persistence?
  • Can a failing or hung smoke stage be diagnosed, return non-zero, and clean up its entire child-process tree?
  • Does CI actually execute both the existing development smoke and the new public-consumer smoke?
  • Are Packagist registration, webhook refresh, and successful clean install verified as distinct steps?
  • Is Framework issue #9 left open until release, public install, runtime, docs build, and evidence are all complete?

docs.title: Tusk Published Application Golden Path
docs.text:
Status: Design and implementation plan approved by the user; implementation in progress.

Decision update: The canonical flow does not include tusk build. The Engine has no built-in build command, and the App skeleton has no Composer build script. The Engine generates RoadRunner configuration as part of tusk start; the project currently has no compilation or package artifact that would justify a separate build step. Revisit a preparation command only when Tusk defines a concrete artifact or production-optimization contract.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Make the supported path from a clean machine to a running Tusk PHP application discoverable, reproducible, and verifiable across the App skeleton, Framework package, Engine, and Docs repositories.

docs.title: User and success criteria
docs.text:
The target user is a PHP developer who has Composer and the Tusk Engine available, but has not cloned or edited Tusk's own repositories. They should be able to create a project from Packagist, understand which component owns each concern, validate the environment, start the application through RoadRunner, and receive an HTTP response from the sample endpoint.

Success means the public Composer command works from a clean temporary directory using stable published packages, the documented Engine commands match the released CLI, the sample endpoint is reachable, and the documentation build succeeds without stale descriptions of the removed native/NDJSON worker architecture.

docs.title: Canonical ownership and flow
Public package identity and release order
docs.text:
• Keep the GitHub repository slug tusk-framework/tusk-app; set the Composer project package name to tusk-framework/app.
  • Register tusk-framework/app on Packagist and configure/verify automatic updates from pushes to its GitHub repository. Do not commit Packagist credentials or webhook secrets.
  • The Framework's current public stable release is 0.3.2. The separately approved removal of its unfinished declarative HTTP/discovery proof of concept is a breaking API cleanup. Respect the repository's configured breaking-change → major release rule; do not silently ship the removal as a patch/minor release.
  • Publish the Framework's resulting stable major release before changing the skeleton to require it. Then update the skeleton's Framework constraint to the new compatible stable major (currently expected to be ^1.0.0 from 0.3.2; confirm the actual release tag before editing the manifest).
  • Do not register/publish an App package while its manifest requires a Framework version that is not yet published.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
1. App repository: update the package identity, version constraint after the Framework major release, README/create-project examples, and manifest tests. Preserve the project type and application code; do not turn the skeleton into a reusable library.
  2. Engine repository: run and, if necessary, strengthen a clean-consumer smoke test that starts from the published Composer skeleton and checks the documented doctor and start lifecycle. Keep RoadRunner as the transport/worker owner. The test must not rely on a local Framework path override or a dev-* dependency.
  3. Docs repository: rewrite the current getting-started path, CLI usage, Engine integration, architecture, and deployment pages to match the canonical flow. Update navigation labels and remove obsolete examples that claim the Engine implements request pools/IPC, NDJSON, a root worker.php, a native HTTP server, or tusk init <name> scaffolding. Keep unrelated guides only where they remain accurate.
  4. Framework issue #9: update its checklist with repository/PR evidence; close only after the clean consumer install, Engine smoke, and documentation build all pass.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Promoting TuskPress into a product; it remains an illustrative sample.
  • Adding an Engine HTTP proxy/gateway, service mesh, native transport, or another worker pool.
  • Reopening intentionally deferred Framework issues #7 or #8.
  • Adding a new public Framework SDK or declarative outbound HTTP client as part of the golden path.
  • Reworking application features unrelated to demonstrating the skeleton and RoadRunner lifecycle.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
1. A clean Composer invocation can create tusk-framework/app without a local path repository, development branch, or copied Framework source.
  2. The resulting project resolves a stable Framework release compatible with the skeleton constraint and passes its manifest validation and test suite.
  3. A clean Engine smoke run can execute the documented CLI lifecycle and reach the sample HTTP endpoint through RoadRunner; failure output identifies the failing stage and preserves non-zero exit status.
  4. The documentation presents one consistent create → diagnose → start → verify path, names the component that owns each step, and makes the Engine/RoadRunner/Framework boundary explicit. It does not advertise a tusk build step until that command has a concrete, separately designed artifact or optimization contract.
  5. mkdocs build --strict succeeds, and a search of active user documentation finds no obsolete Native Engine/NDJSON/worker.php runtime claims or unsupported tusk init <name> project-generation examples.
  6. Packagist contains the matching tusk-framework/app package and the GitHub push-update mechanism is verified with a successful package metadata refresh; an HTTP webhook acknowledgement alone is not considered proof of index refresh.
  7. Framework issue #9 is closed only after links to the merged App/Engine/Docs PRs and the above verification evidence are recorded.

docs.title: Rollout and dependencies
docs.text: The implementation is split into repository PRs. First merge and release the Framework breaking cleanup. Then update and register the App skeleton against that stable release. In parallel, update Docs and prepare the Engine clean-consumer smoke once the package is publicly resolvable. Run the final golden-path check from an empty directory, record evidence on issue #9, and close it last. If Packagist registration or indexing is blocked, keep the relevant PR open and report the external prerequisite rather than substituting a local path repository.

docs.title: Risks and mitigations
docs.text:
• Packagist identity or indexing mismatch: verify the exact Composer name and clean public install before treating the path as complete.
  • Breaking-version mismatch: read the actual published Framework tag and test the App constraint against it before publishing the skeleton package.
  • Docs drift: validate every command against Engine CLI behavior and the App README; require a strict MkDocs build.
  • Flaky end-to-end runtime checks: bound startup/readiness time, collect Engine/RoadRunner logs on failure, and use deterministic cleanup in the smoke harness.
